segments.text: Male Speaker:  Ladies and gentlemen,
please welcome the Vice President
of the United States,  J.D. Vance.
(applause)
The Vice President:  Good morning.
Thank you all. Well, good morning to the press,
and good morning to all the people
who've worked so hard on this.
This is a great day for American workers,
because we are taking some very concrete actions
to cut down on some of the H-1b and J-1 visa fraud
that we've been tracking over the past several months.
I want to give a particular shout out to Andrew Ferguson,
Stephen Miller, and of course, Todd Blanche,
our great attorney general, who are standing behind me.
A particular shout out to DOL Secretary Keith Sonderling,
who's been really an amazing partner
in the anti-fraud task force. Thanks to Keith's hard work,
we've uncovered about $20 billion in fraud
just within his department
and secured over 200 convictions in the last five months alone.
So, Keith has been one of our real all-stars
on the anti-fraud task force.
And of course, the IG of DOL, Anthony Esposito,
all of them will speak
and then you guys can ask us a few questions.
But here's the basic problem,
something that we've been working towards
fixing in the Trump administration for a long time.
The H-1b visa program is meant to allow companies to bring
in really the best of the best
from outside the United States of America for positions
that are completely impossible to fill with American workers.
Unfortunately, the program has become rife with fraud
over the last several years,
probably the last several decades.
And here's the basic game that American corporations
and foreign corporations will play -- they will say --
maybe they'll put an advertisement
in a small-town newspaper.
They'll go out there and say that we have advertised
for a position with our company, and nobody is responding to it.
And they will use that lack of response
to then go and replace American workers
with what is effectively foreign indentured servants.
And I'll get into that in a second.
But these are not people who are coming into
the United States of America, these H-1b visas,
with the full rights of an American citizen
or an American employee.
They're coming in and being mistreated by their employers
and being used to undercut the wages of American workers.
Now, there are two ways this system fundamentally works.
The H-1b visa is how the people get into the United States
in the first place.
And then a PERM program is how those employees stay.
So, after a couple of cycles of H-1b reapplication,
the companies will then apply for a PERM,
a P-E-R-M,
which will allow the employee to stay, get a green card,
and potentially stay in the United States indefinitely.
So, if the H-1b visa is how people come into the country,
the PERM program is how they stay in the United States
to begin with.
Now, there has been no company in the United States,
unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft
and let me just give you a couple of statistics on this.
So, in the last year, Microsoft --
and I want to be clear about the data here,
so let me check this.
But Microsoft laid off last year 6,000 -- 6,000 American workers.
At the same time, the company benefited from 6,300 H-1b visas
and almost 3,000 green cards.
In other words, if you do the math for every worker
that Microsoft laid off,
they replaced that worker with one
and a half foreign indentured servants.
Now, that is a scandalous system that we've allowed
in this country for far too long.
But thanks to the work of this task force,
and thanks to the empowerment of the president
of the United States, we are going to stop it.
Because, thanks to an ongoing investigation,
we have decided to suspend the PERM program for Microsoft,
which means they will no longer be able to apply --
they'll no longer be able to take those H-1bs
and apply for permanent resident status
within the United States of America.
Now, our message to Microsoft and to any other foreign
or domestic corporation is quite simple --
we obviously want you to thrive in the United States of America.
We want people to invest in the United States of America,
particularly the American technology sector.
We are the biggest boosters of your industry.
We want you to continue to grow and to employ a lot of people,
but we want you to employ American workers.
And so, our message to Microsoft is,
you're a great American company,
but you've got to hire great American workers.
You cannot lay off American workers
and then replace them with foreign indentured servants.
And I want to talk a little bit about that.
When I say indentured servants, here's what I mean --
when somebody comes in on an H-1b,
they are completely --
they're completely subordinate to that company.
If they lose that job, they have to leave the country.
So, if you think of the basic idea
of an American constitutional republic
where we bring people in who are fair
and equal citizens of the United States of America,
they are not controlled by their employer.
But you bring people in and you basically tell them
that if they get out of line, if they get too uppity at work,
they're not just going to lose their job,
but they're going to be deported back
to their country of residence.
Those people are not full citizens,
and that's why those people are earning wages
that are far below the average for American citizens.
The second thing I want to say about that is this fraud
is facilitated not just by the companies themselves,
but in some ways is facilitated
by these foreign outsourcing firms,
these firms that help corporations apply
and find H-1b visa candidates.
They're commonly called the witches,
the four major outsourcing firms.
And these firms are as complicit,
or maybe more so complicit,
in the visa fraud than any American corporation
and here's the basic data.
If you are working as an H-1b visa
in the United States of America, you're earning $20,000
less than an American citizen hired in the same position.
If you were brought in by one of these foreign outsourcing firms,
you're making $48,000 less than an American citizen
in a similar position.
So, I'm sure that everybody here understands the game
that is being played; you bring in indentured servants
from outside the country, you lay off American workers.
And if you're a corporation, you make a ton of money
by undercutting the wages of American workers,
replacing them with people who, frankly, shouldn't be
in the United States of America to begin with.
This is a terribly pernicious system,
it's gone on for too long,
and we'd all encourage, by the way,
Congress to do something about it.
But there are things within our authority under the law,
our regulatory authorities and administration
to fix this problem
and that's exactly what we're going to do.
I want to make one final announcement here,
because while we see a lot of H-1b visa fraud,
we also see a lot of J-1 visa fraud.
And this is where some of America's most elite
universities bring in foreigners, again,
to undercut the wages of American residents.
Now, there are nine universities in particular
that we believe merit an investigation.
Those universities are Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown,
the University of Pittsburgh,
UC Davis, Caltech, Arizona State and MIT.
And what we see is that when you employ an American worker,
as a graduate student, as a researcher,
they're making about $20,000
more than someone brought in under a J-1 visa.
And importantly,
these universities are employing J-1 visas
for federally funded grants at a rate of about 61 percent.
The national average is 38 percent.
So, something weird is going on at these universities.
They're using these visas way too much,
they're using them to undercut the wages
of American grad students and American researchers,
and it simply has to stop.
Let me make one final point before I turn it over to Keith.
This is a fundamental insult to the American worker
and to the American way of life.
We cannot allow visa programs that were designed to ensure
that American corporations had access to the best
and the brightest,
to use them to undercut the wages of American workers.
Now, it's one thing, if you want to bring in a person
like Elon Musk,
I think 99 percent of American citizens
look at somebody like Elon Musk or Lisa Su, the CEO of AMD,
and they say, obviously, if that person wants to come in
and build something great in the United States of America,
we support that.
But if you're bringing in an accountant
who's making $40,000 a year,
and you use that for an indentured servant
making $40,000 a year to replace an American worker
who was making $70,000 a year, you're not bringing in a genius
to build a great American corporation;
you're committing fraud against the American people
and against this visa program.
It has to stop and, thanks to the work of this task force,
and again,
the empowerment of the president of the United States,
we are doing something to stop it.
I, again, would encourage Congress to reform this program;
it is very clear that it's not working the way that it should.
But we have tools in the administration
to make this program work better for the American people.
A lot more we could do
if Congress was willing to play ball.
And again, we extend an invitation
to both Democrats and Republicans.
If you want the H-1b visa program
to stop being used to defraud the American taxpayer
and to undercut the wages of American workers,
get to work, and we will help you.
But we're going to do everything that we can in the interim
to ensure the program works as it was designed to work.
And with that, I want to turn it over to our great
Labor Secretary, Keith, take it away.
Keith Sonderling: Well, thank you,
Vice President Vance,
for the task force and all the task force members
for the amazing work we do together.
Because of this task force, the Department of Labor
has uncovered $22 billion in visa fraud.
But today, we are protecting something far more valuable
than any dollar amount --
we are protecting the American worker.
The Department of Labor is taking historic action
by shutting down the pipeline of systemic fraud,
the fraud that has flooded our country with foreign labor
at the expense of American workers.
It begins with universities and companies
that have turned into visa mills,
promoting foreign workers that have lied
about their qualifications
to take jobs from our beloved American workers.
But these foreign workers aren't coming here just for the job.
Employers have enabled this pipeline through fraud,
putting foreign labor ahead of American workers.
And the fraud doesn't end with getting the job;
that job becomes a pathway for foreign workers
and their families to stay in America permanently
and eventually becoming US citizens.
And who pays for it all? The American worker.
This administration knows that American workers
are the best and brightest in the world.
These jobs that were stolen from them should have gone
and will now go to Americans first, not foreigners,
and especially not foreign fraudsters.
And today, thanks to President Trump, the vice president,
and the task force,
we are cutting off the head of the snake.
The companies that have enabled this abuse for decades,
due to ongoing criminal investigations
led by the Department of Labors' Inspector General,
Anthony D'Esposito, who will get into this shortly,
I am hereby suspending
from the Permanent Labor Certification Program
some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world:
Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini.
And also, due to multiple active federal investigations,
the Department of Labor is suspending Microsoft
and Adobe from the program. So, what does this mean?
We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent
labor certification applications involving these companies.
Since 2009, just these companies alone
have requested almost 3 million foreign workers.
They've received over 230,000 H-1b visas approvals,
and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications.
That's hundreds of thousands of jobs
that were taken from American workers.
Our historic action is the first critical step
to stop the fraud and the abuse and ensure that these programs
never come at the expense of the American worker.
Under President Trump's leadership,
and thanks to Vice President Vance
and this task force, we are ending the fraud
that has fueled reliance on foreign labor.
President Trump's Department of Labor
will ensure that American businesses now
look first to the most talented workforce in the world,
and that's the American worker.
Thank you and now I invite Attorney General Blanche
to the stage.
Todd Blanche: Thank you very much, Keith,
and congratulations on your recent confirmation.
So, this announcement today should send
and does send a strong signal
to every single employer in the United States
that the Trump administration
will not tolerate discrimination against American workers.
For too long, employers have engaged in tactics,
as you've just heard from the vice president
and Secretary Sonderling, to protect,
and in some cases, prefer, foreign workers
for all types of job opportunities.
These practices have shut American workers
out of the economy of their own country
and have made it more difficult
for both recent college graduates
and also experienced workers to get a fair shake
at the employment market and a fair wage, but no longer.
I want to thank the Department of Justice,
the folks that work in the Civil Rights Division
and the Department of Labor and their IG's office.
You're going to hear from the Inspector General in a moment,
and also the other members of the task force
that have worked so hard over the past several months
to get where we are today.
And just let me make clear, if it's not clear,
the Department of Justice, my department,
is actively investigating companies that do this,
that favor foreign workers over the American people.
The American people have spoken loud and clear --
if a company, even including Microsoft, Adobe or any other,
discriminates against an American worker
in favor of someone on the other side of the world,
that company has violated the trust of the federal government
and the American people and will be investigated.
This issue has affected Americans across generations,
but it's especially important to young people
with a lot of talent who can't find a job
because their potential employer may be engaging
in these sorts of improper and nefarious practices.
I want to thank the vice president
and Secretary Sonderling for their leadership on this issue.
It's an honor to be a part of the administration
that takes this issue seriously.
The issue of foreign labor favoritism
is something that nobody should ignore.
And we at the Department of Justice will continue
to do our part to make sure that doesn't happen.
Thank you very much. I'll now turn it over to Stephen Miller.
Thank you very much.
Stephen Miller: Good morning, everybody.
thank you, Mr. Vice President, for your leadership,
not only on this issue,
but the entire body of work the Fraud Task Force has done.
Since President Trump launched the Fraud Task Force
and put the vice president in charge,
our worst nightmares about the fraud
that had been taking place in this country were exceeded,
fraud that has been going on for years,
decades, in some cases generations.
Vice President Vance and his team
have exposed historic volumes of food stamp fraud,
daycare fraud, Medicaid fraud,
health care fraud, Social Security fraud,
every kind of fraud you can imagine
that steals from and betrays American families and workers.
Today is no different; what the task force
and its partners in law enforcement
have uncovered is systemic immigration fraud
that violates the laws and statutes of the United States
to undercut American workers and labor.
The H-1b program and the PERM program that's attached
to it have explicit statutory commands that must be followed.
It requires individuals, for example, to have a unique,
highly specialized occupation, as one example.
And yet, in case after case after case,
we see individuals that are being brought into the country
for skills that are not specialized,
that are not unique, and that are not skilled,
and that are doing work that is currently being done
by American workers, but at vastly lower pay.
If you go back a few decades in this country,
this was an issue that was covered commonly by our media.
In fact, there's a famous special
that was done by Mike Wallace at CBS
probably almost 30 years ago now,
when this program was first starting, documenting
and detailing these abuses. If you remember, in 2015,
when President Trump first campaigned for President,
he had at his rallies American workers in good paying,
middle-class jobs with pensions who were laid off
and forced to train their foreign replacements
as a condition of their severance,
a phenomenon that is widespread and well documented.
And again, because of this task force,
this kind of unlawful conduct has been exposed,
detailed, documented,
and resulted in real, concrete federal action.
I think one of the important things
that I would like everyone to take home today
is that America is blessed
with some of the most exceptional talent
that has ever existed in the history of the world --
homegrown American talent.
This has been true since the day our country was founded.
Go back to the Wright Brothers and the journey into the skies;
the industrial base that powered us through World War II;
the genius of American spaceflight and aviation.
Homegrown American talent has been at the center
of one revolution after another.
As the Vice President said, we always welcome
and bring to this country individuals
who have exceptional gifts to share with our country.
But what we don't do and can't do is crush
and kill the dreams of millions of young children
in middle school and high school
who want that first step in the ladder
but are unable to get it, or mid-career workers
who dedicated their lives to a company
and are given two weeks' notice just because someone else,
somewhere in the world is willing to do the job 20,
30, 40, 50 percent cheaper than they are.
And a lot of the reason why they can do it so much cheaper
is they are able to then
go back to their home countries in the future
and, if they're living in a country
where the average salary is $2 a day or $3 a day,
taking half of an American worker's salary
is still a raise in their home country.
The last thing I want to say is that there's been
a lot of attention given to how President Trump
has secured the southern border of the United States,
which is the most significant security achievement
in American history.
In other words, the most open border
to the most secure border in the span of days.
Nothing has equaled that since this country was founded
in terms of a security achievement.
But what President Trump has done to fix
and reform the immigration system more broadly
is equally as astonishing and impressive.
He completely fixed and repaired the refugee program;
he battled the issue of visa overstays for the first time
ever and created a program all throughout the world
to ensure people are abiding by
and obeying the rules of their stay.
He cracked down for the first time ever on birth tourism,
something that has been a scourge
and an embarrassment for years.
He dealt with the issue of immigration
from terrorist havens and dangerous nations
with the travel bans and travel restrictions.
He's applied the public charge standard for the first time
ever to ensure people who are coming to this country
are not going to be seeking or reliant on welfare.
He's dealt with systemic fraud
across every different visa program that exists,
generations of work done in less than two years
so that it is true today that under President Trump,
America is the only country in the world
that has managed to turn an immigration system
from being against its people to for its people.
And in particular in the Western world,
where this has been simmering for a long time,
President Trump is the only Western leader
to deliver for the citizens of this country,
an immigration system that puts them first.
No other Western leader has done this;
President Trump stands alone.
I'd now love to have Mr. D'Esposito,
the Inspector General of Labor, take the stage.
Thank you.
Anthony D'Esposito: Thank you very much, Steve,
and thank you for your leadership and commitment.
Under President Donald Trump and Vice President JD
Vance, fraud is no longer being dismissed
as an accounting error. Fraud is a crime.
Fraud steals American jobs. Fraud fuels violence.
Fraud threatens our national security.
President Trump and Vice President Vance understand
that protecting America means standing behind the men
and women who wear the uniform,
giving them the resources to do their jobs,
and letting cops be cops.
Alongside my partner, Secretary Keith Sonderling,
I am announcing a historic investigation
into the J-1 visa fraud
involving nine major American universities:
Pitt, Yale, Harvard, Sanford-Brown, UC Davis,
Caltech, Arizona State and MIT.
Subpoenas have been served, investigations are underway,
and nobody will be getting a free pass
because their name is carved into an expensive building.
Improperly used J-1 visa classifications
to avoid employment obligations, exploit taxpayer funded programs
and undermine American workers will not be tolerated.
Approximately 61 percent postdoctoral researchers
and federally funded workers at these institutions
are foreign nationals.
American taxpayers send billions of dollars to these universities
to support research and innovation.
They deserve to know where that money is --
where it's going, and whether it's being used lawfully.
And China, the Chinese Communist Party doesn't need
to kick down the doors of America's research laboratories
if our own institutions
are willing to leave the doors wide open.
China is not simply an economic competitor;
the Chinese Communist Party is a sophisticated adversary
actively targeting American technology,
intellectual property and national security interests.
We will investigate whether foreign influence,
improper financial relationships or visa abuse
are compromising federally funded research.
If an American university is breaking the law
to save a dollar while exposing American research
to a foreign adversary, that is not academic excellence,
it's institutional betrayal.
Let me make something else crystal clear;
I spent a career as an NYPD detective.
I worked the streets of Brooklyn investigating violent criminals
who thought that they were untouchable.
I did not back down then,
and I sure as hell will not back down now.
I don't care how prestigious a university thinks it is;
break the law and screw the American people
and I will personally cuff you in the University Square.
I don't care how large your endowment is,
how powerful your alumni are,
or how many politicians you have on speed dial.
As Vice President Vance said, nobody is above the law.
That's why we're establishing a visa fraud strike team,
bringing together investigative expertise
from across government.
We will follow the money, uncover the schemes
and work with Attorney General Todd Blanche
to prosecute criminals.
We are also launching a Labor Inspector General Most Wanted
Fraudster List, featuring 16 criminals
who have stolen nearly $0.5 billion from Americans.
To those fugitives, as AG Blanche's team has said,
they will find you anywhere on this planet,
and our results speak for themselves.
Since Vice President Vance's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud
was established,
our investigations have contributed to 171 indictments,
203 convictions, 80 arrests, more than 70 search warrants,
and over $1 billion identified for the taxpayers
and we're just getting started.
During my time wearing an NYPD shield,
I learned that crime doesn't happen in a vacuum.
Fraud doesn't end with a stolen dollar.
That dollar can become a gun in someone's hand,
narcotics that kill, a payment to a human trafficker
or resources for a foreign enemy.
That's why we're investigating the connections between fraud,
organized crime, forced labor, human trafficking,
and threats to national security.
President Trump and Vice President Vance
have unleashed the resources, empowered law enforcement,
and made it clear that protecting American workers
and taxpayers is a national priority.
To the hard-working men of -- the hardworking men and women
of the Labor Inspector General's office,
you have my full support,
and we will give you every tool you need to get the job done.
Anyone exploiting our immigration system,
stealing taxpayer dollars,
or compromising American security,
your university's reputation will not protect you.
Your political connections will not protect you.
Your money will not protect you.
The only thing that matters is the evidence
that we will bring to prosecutions.
President Trump demands America First,
and we, this task force, is delivering.
No amount too small, no fraud too large,
and absolutely no institution above the law.
And now it's my honor to introduce the co-chair
of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud,
Andrew Ferguson.
Andrew Ferguson: Good morning.
America is not a jobs program for the rest of the world.
We didn't build our institutions for the rest of the world;
we built them for Americans.
Our rule of law, our system of sane and sound regulation,
our capital markets, our justice system,
everything that makes the American economy thrive
we did not build for the planet, we built it for us.
We built it for Americans first.
The fraud described today denies Americans that institution.
And that is what the fraud that the task force
has spent the last nine months
uncovering has consistently done,
it denies Americans of their own patrimony.
Benefits fraud denies
Americans their Medicaid and Medicare benefits.
SNAP takes the food out of the mouths of children.
CDL fraud denies Americans a safe road.
Immigration fraud denies the Americans the right
to decide who will be citizens,
fellow citizens of their country.
And this fraud denies Americans their just wage,
a sin that cries out to heaven for vengeance.
That is why this task force is so important.
Fraud of every kind is a frontal assault
on every institution that Americans hold dear.
And if we do not confront it,
those institutions will keep eroding,
our benefits programs will disappear,
Americans will lose their livelihoods,
our roads will be unsafe, crime will continue to rise.
Only President Trump and Vice President
Vance have ever taken these problems seriously.
They have deployed the entire federal government to stop it
and that is ultimately what this is today.
This is protecting institutions
that Americans built for Americans
and preserving them for Americans.
That is why this announcement is so huge.
I also want to acknowledge the work of Andrea Lucas,
who is the chairman of the EEOC.
She is the greatest chairman of that institution
since Clarence Thomas back in the 1980s.
On every issue that previous EEOCs refused to touch,
protecting white American men from discrimination,
protecting American citizens
from national origin, discrimination.
She has led the EEOC headlong to defend Americans
from these abusive practices.
She has been an incredibly valuable partner
of the task force.
I know she's been a very valuable partner
of the Department of Justice,
and we are thrilled to work with her on these issues.
And with that, I will return it to the vice president.
The Vice President: So, let me just echo
what Andrew just said about Andrea Lucas
and, of course, Harmeet Dhillon,
who have been amazing partners in this work,
and it wouldn't be impossible without them.
We finally have an administration,
a Department of Justice led by Todd Blanche,
who are taking seriously that American citizens
have rights in their own country.
It sounds like a novel concept,
but for so long we sent a message to people,
whether they were white or male or the wrong national origin,
we said that we were going to defend your rights
if you looked the wrong way,
or you didn't belong to the right category.
No more in this administration
and that's because of the hard work
of Harmeet Dhillon and Andrea Lucas.
Let me make one final point.
There's this pernicious idea, and Stephen alluded to it,
which is that Americans are not good enough
for the jobs in their own country.
You hear people say that in subtle ways
and sometimes explicit ways.
When people say that Americans won't work on farms
or they won't work in certain dirty jobs,
what they're really saying is that Americans won't work
on those jobs for poverty wages, nor should they.
When you hear people say
that we have to bring in foreign accountants
because there aren't enough American accountants,
what they're saying is that there aren't enough people
who can do math in the United States of America,
which is absurd.
When people say we need to bring in foreign IT specialists
and quite literally force people to train their own replacements,
what we're saying is that there are Americans
who cannot do those jobs, and that is absurd.
To the American people this visa fraud is a frontal assault
on the idea that you deserve to inherit the jobs
and the positions in your own country.
Never believe the lie that Americans are not good enough
to build a future for Americans.
That is what visa fraud tells you; it is a lie,
and the president of the United States does not stand for it,
and neither does anybody on this stage.
Thank you. Go ahead. Go ahead.
The Press: Thank you very much.
I wanted to ask, you had some harsh words for Microsoft
at the top of your speech just then,
yet, in that case, why is President Trump
awarding the nation's top technological medal
to the CEO of Microsoft this afternoon?
The Vice President: Well, like I said,
Microsoft is a great American company,
and we have a great relationship with them,
they do a lot of important things.
They also laid off 6,000 American workers
while replacing them with 6,300 h-1bs.
And our message to Microsoft
is not that we want to harm your company,
it's that we want your company to thrive,
but we want it to thrive by employing
and empowering your fellow Americans.
So, we're going to continue to support Microsoft
and have a great relationship with Microsoft,
but we're also going to deny them the ability
to apply for these permanent residencies
until they show that they're going to get serious
about putting American workers first.
Go ahead. Yeah.
In the orange and then the red.
The Press: Thank you.
So, assuming that a lot of these people have --
they brought families over,
this is kind of a two-part question,
if they brought families over
and they were living in high-cost living areas.
So, were those families then eligible for social benefits,
SNAP benefits, educational benefits?
If that's the case, because of the lower cost,
because they weren't being paid as much,
is the federal government
going to be holding some of these companies liable for that
to try to recoup some of that money that was on --
basically at the taxpayers' expense?
The Vice President: Well, in some cases,
we actually already have tried to ensure
that if you're coming to the United States of America
and benefiting from our very generous welfare system,
that you should stop doing that.
We've seen that in some of the mortgage application programs
that we have;
we've seen that in a number of other programs as well.
So, yes, I mean, our message to newcomers
to the United States of America,
whatever program they're coming on,
is that you should come to the United States
to enrich this country, to make this country better,
to participate, of course,
in the institutions of American democracy.
If your purpose in coming to the United States of America
is to cash a check, meaning a check not for working,
but from our generous welfare program,
then you're not going to enrich the United States of America,
and we would prefer that you not come here.
The Press: Are you going to be going after some of these?
The Vice President: We're going to continue to look
at a number of these things.
Again, we've already done some of this work,
but we're going to continue to look at ways
of recouping American taxpayer money
that has effectively gone to subsidize cheap labor
all over the United States of America.
The Press: Thank you so much, Mr. Vice President.
Cara Castronuova, Lindell TV.
